trust_decision.summary: The router decides which route (and so which route-level middleware, e.g. auth) applies by matching the raw still-encoded path; the static file resolvers then decode the wildcard and must not let a decoded separator reach a file outside the path the router authorised.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'encoded slash ... exposes static files'; StaticDirectoryHandler (behind e.Static/e.StaticFS) is the obvious place where the wildcard is PathUnescaped and then opened.

fix_sites.entry_point: e.Static / e.StaticFS / g.Static / g.StaticFS / public echo.StaticDirectoryHandler (HTTP GET <prefix>*)
same handler; filepath.Clean -> path.Clean so %5C-decoded backslash stays literal on Windows
middleware.Static / StaticWithConfig mounted on a group or wildcard route (c.Path() ends with '*')
fix_sites.module_kind: middleware package (second implementation of static serving)

fix_sites.entry_point: new internal helper internal/pathutil.HasEncodedPathSeparator shared by both sites

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: middleware/static.go:198-219 (Static middleware resolves files itself, independent of echo.StaticDirectoryHandler at echo.go:588)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The middleware branch that reads the already-decoded URL.Path carries a fresh comment that it 'must not be unescaped again' (#2599), and the router-unescape mode is an explicit opt-in (UnescapePathParamValues + DisablePathUnescaping), so a solver can argue both are 'nothing to unescape here' or 'user's chosen configuration'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: File names containing a literal '%' (encoded as %25, e.g. 100%25.txt) and double-encoded %252F must still be served as literal names; rejecting any '%' or decoding twice breaks #2599 behaviour. Also directory redirect for real directories and the HTML5/next() fall-through must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: backslash treated literally via path.Clean instead of filepath.Clean (Windows)
%252F double-encoded must stay a literal filename (not rejected as separator)

O7_producer.where: Route-match path chosen in router.go:797-803 (RawPath vs Path) and param values optionally unescaped at router.go:1025-1033; this is routing state, not a schema/serializer/cache

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Static middleware via e.Use/e.Pre with no wildcard route matched: p is taken from the already-decoded URL.Path, so /admin%2Fsecret.txt misses the /admin/* group (router matched raw path) yet the middleware opens admin/secret.txt; the fix only guards the pathUnescape branch.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Comment says URL.Path is already decoded by net/http and must not be unescaped (#2599); the check sits inside 'if pathUnescape' so the branch looks unaffected.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (middleware) from landing point echo.go; needs knowledge that e.Use middleware runs after routing (echo.go:367-375) and that routing used RawPath (router.go:797-803)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Router configured with UnescapePathParamValues=true plus StaticDirectoryHandler(fs, true) or StaticConfig{DisablePathUnescaping:true}: router matched the raw path but hands a decoded wildcard containing '/', and the new check is skipped because it sits inside the !disablePathUnescaping branch.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Documented as the configuration where 'router is already unescaping', an explicit opt-in combination, so the solver argues it is the user's choice / unsupported combination.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: router.go (core) vs both static resolvers; the decoding happens in the router, a different layer from the check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a FileFS-based helper/route that serves c.Param("*") after url.PathUnescape without the separator check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: c.FileFS/fsFile is the shared primitive; a maintainer adding a convenience 'serve wildcard from fs' API would naturally copy the unescape+Clean idiom from echo.go:591-600.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: IgnoreBase path rewriting computed from decoded p, which could reintroduce a separator split after the check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Existing string surgery on filePath after decoding; a parser differential on the item identity (how-type).
